- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.7) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤-0.3) or volatile, model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–4% if recent price is falling.  
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days); apply “lag correction” — reduce forecast by 2–5% for 3–7 days post-spike.  
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 50% of 30d moving avg), model tends to hold too high; lower forecast by 2–5% for next 7–14 days.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates early in the forecast window (first 5–7 days); apply “early bias correction” — reduce first 5 days by 1–3% if sentiment is neutral or negative.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated “reversal” patterns (e.g., +0.3 → -0.3 → +0.3), model tends to mispredict direction; use sentiment momentum to weight next 3–5 days’ forecast.
